rag_chunks.text: Sun safety is always in season. It’s important to protect your skin from sun damage throughout the year, no matter what the weather. Exposing your skin to the sun year-round means you are exposing it to ultraviolet radiation, which can cause sunburn, early skin aging (such as skin spots, wrinkles, or “leathery skin”), eye damage, and skin cancer, the most common form of cancer in the U.S. Sunscreen is one of several ways to help reduce the risk of skin cancer. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration continues to evaluate sunscreen products to ensure they are safe and effective. Although all sunscreens help protect against sunburn, only broad-spectrum sunscreens with a sun protection factor (SPF) of at least 15 help protect against the UV rays that increase the risk of skin cancer and early skin aging caused by the sun. Broad-spectrum sunscreens protect against both UVA and UVB rays.
rag_chunks.locator: Consumer article, passage beginning “Sun safety is always in season.…”
rag_chunks.limitations: 관할 기관의 소비자 안내다. 실제 제품의 사용법과 내수성 표시를 함께 확인한다.

### 근거 및 이유
흐린 하늘에서도 야외 자외선 노출이 없어지지 않아요. 두 번 다 일어날 예정인 노출이라면 외출 준비에서 둘 다 고려할 수 있어요. [ref:sun_protection-015]
